definition: having a harmful effect, especially in a way that is gradual and hard to notice

collocations.example: Social media can have a pernicious effect on young people's self-esteem.
It is a pernicious myth that hard work always guarantees success.

definition: meeting a line or surface at an angle of 90 degrees

collocations.example: The new road runs perpendicular to the main highway.
The students drew two perpendicular lines that crossed at the center.

definition: to read or look through something carefully

collocations.example: Take your time to peruse the document before signing it.
A copy of the catalog is available to peruse at your leisure.

definition: the basic unit of money in Mexico and several other Latin American countries

collocations.example: The Mexican peso weakened sharply against the US dollar this week.
The peso fell to a record low on the currency markets.

definition: a feeling that bad things will happen and that a situation will not improve

collocations.example: A mood of pessimism spread through the office after the layoffs.
There is growing pessimism about the company's chances of survival.

definition: (of a woman) attractively small and slim

collocations.example: She is a petite woman who still looks graceful in heels.
She is petite but surprisingly strong for her size.

definition: to make someone so frightened that they cannot move or think

collocations.example: The thought of public speaking seems to petrify many students.
She is petrified of spiders and screams whenever she sees one.

definition: a ruler of ancient Egypt

collocations.example: The museum displays treasures buried with an ancient pharaoh.
Archaeologists spent years searching for the lost pharaoh's tomb.

definition: the philosophical study of human experience and consciousness

collocations.example: Her lecture explored the phenomenology of everyday perception.
He went to graduate school to study phenomenology and modern philosophy.

definition: used in the names of orchestras and groups that perform classical music

collocations.example: The city's philharmonic orchestra performed Beethoven's famous Ninth Symphony.
She dreamed of one day conducting the Berlin Philharmonic.

definition: a strong, unreasonable fear of something

collocations.example: He has a phobia about flying and avoids long trips.
She developed a phobia of enclosed spaces after the accident.

definition: relating to the sounds of human speech

collocations.example: Pilots use the phonetic alphabet to spell words clearly over the radio.
The dictionary gives a phonetic transcription for every headword.

definition: a chemical element that is important for living things and is used in fertilizers and matches

collocations.example: The match tips are coated with a layer of red phosphorus.
Plants need nitrogen and phosphorus to grow healthy and strong.

definition: the process by which green plants use sunlight to make food from water and carbon dioxide

collocations.example: During the process of photosynthesis, plants release oxygen into the air.
The weak indoor lighting was not strong enough to support photosynthesis.

definition: the shape and size of a person's body

collocations.example: Years of swimming gave him a lean, athletic physique.
He has the physique of a man half his age.

definition: done gradually in separate stages rather than all at one time

collocations.example: A piecemeal approach to the problem will only waste time.
These piecemeal solutions will not fix the deeper issue.

definition: a person who plays a pipe or the bagpipes

collocations.example: A lone piper played a sad tune at the funeral.
A skilled piper entertained the crowd at the village festival.

definition: the illegal copying or selling of someone else's work, such as software, music, or films

collocations.example: The company lost millions of dollars because of software piracy.
New laws were introduced to combat piracy of movies online.

definition: to make someone less angry or upset by doing something to please them

collocations.example: The new policy did little to placate the company's critics.
He offered a free meal to placate the angry customer.

definition: cloth with a pattern of crossed lines and squares in different colors

collocations.example: He wore a red plaid shirt and faded blue jeans.
The blanket was woven in a traditional plaid pattern.

definition: a game or series of games played to decide the winner of a competition

collocations.example: They lost the crucial playoff game by a single point.
The team needs two more wins to reach the playoffs.

definition: a very large amount of something, often more than is needed

collocations.example: The new website offers a plethora of options for travelers.
The new manager faced a plethora of problems on her first day.

definition: to walk slowly and heavily, especially because you are tired

collocations.example: The exhausted hikers plodded along the muddy mountain path.
We plodded through the deep snow for nearly an hour.

definition: a serious infectious disease that can cause paralysis, especially in children

collocations.example: The polio vaccine has saved millions of children from paralysis.
He was crippled by polio as a young child.

definition: a society or country that has an organized form of government

collocations.example: The country slowly grew into a stable, democratic polity.
A free and active press protects the health of the polity.

definition: a person whose job is to carry out opinion polls

collocations.example: A leading pollster predicted a close result in the election.
Pollsters predict that the mayor will win a second term.

definition: a small lump that grows on the inside of the body, such as in the nose or intestine

collocations.example: The doctor removed a nasal polyp to help him breathe better.
Surgeons were able to remove the polyp during a routine procedure.

definition: a tall, fast-growing tree with soft wood

collocations.example: A row of poplar trees lined the quiet country road.
They planted a row of poplars to block the strong wind.

definition: all the ordinary people who live in a particular country or area

collocations.example: The new mayor had the strong support of the local populace.
The policy was deeply unpopular with the general populace.

definition: a soft food made by boiling oats or rice in milk or water

collocations.example: She ate a warm bowl of porridge every winter morning.
The restaurant serves rice porridge with pickled vegetables for breakfast.

definition: a group of people who come together, especially to support or help someone

collocations.example: A posse of reporters followed the actor down the street.
Her friends formed a posse to cheer her through treatment.

definition: happening, given, or published after a person has died

collocations.example: The soldier received a posthumous award for his bravery.
The posthumous publication of her diary became a bestseller.

definition: relating to the period of time after a surgical operation

collocations.example: Good postoperative care helps patients recover more quickly after surgery.
The nurse gave her medicine to control the postoperative pain.

definition: a practical way of dealing with problems based on real situations rather than fixed ideas

collocations.example: Her political pragmatism helped her win support from both parties.
The talks succeeded because of a shared spirit of pragmatism.

definition: a small sea animal with a shell that is cooked and eaten

collocations.example: The chef grilled a few king prawns for the appetizer.
She ordered a prawn cocktail to start her meal.

definition: a rule or principle that guides how people should behave

collocations.example: Honesty is a basic precept of good business practice.
He tried to follow the precept of treating others fairly.

definition: the largest part or greatest amount of something

collocations.example: A preponderance of evidence pointed to the defendant's guilt.
The preponderance of opinion favored building the new library.

definition: completely unreasonable or silly; ridiculous

collocations.example: The idea that she stole the money is absolutely preposterous.
He made the preposterous claim that he had never slept.

definition: a false reason given to hide the real one

collocations.example: He left early on the pretext of having work to do.
The incident gave the government a pretext for canceling the vote.

definition: very formal and proper in behavior, and easily shocked by rude things

collocations.example: She was far too prim and proper to tell such jokes.
The teacher spoke in a prim manner that discouraged questions.

definition: existing from the very beginning, especially of the earth or universe

collocations.example: Life may have begun in a warm primordial soup of chemicals.
Millions of years ago, dense primordial forest covered the valley.

definition: a transparent glass or plastic object that breaks light into the colors of the rainbow

collocations.example: Sunlight passing through a triangular prism forms a bright rainbow.
When light shines through a prism, it splits into many colors.

definition: very large, powerful, or impressive

collocations.example: The factory produces a prodigious amount of waste each day.
The young pianist showed prodigious talent at an early age.

definition: a young person with exceptional talent or ability

collocations.example: She was a child prodigy who gave concerts at seven.
The musical prodigy composed his first symphony at twelve.

definition: showing a lack of respect for God or for sacred things

collocations.example: The coach was fined for using profane language during the game.
Fans were warned not to make profane gestures at the players.

definition: to offer something such as advice, help, or an explanation

collocations.example: She was always ready to proffer advice to new employees.
He proffered an explanation for his late arrival at work.

definition: the group of ordinary working people, especially those who earn wages doing physical work

collocations.example: The factory system created a large industrial proletariat in the cities.
Marx wrote about the dictatorship of the proletariat as a political goal.

definition: a separate introduction at the beginning of a book, play, or film

collocations.example: The prologue to the novel is written as a newspaper report.
The author added a brief prologue explaining how the story began.

definition: a formal dance party held for students, especially at the end of high school

collocations.example: She was thrilled when he asked her to the prom.
The students rented a limousine for their big prom night.

definition: the force that pushes a vehicle or object forward

collocations.example: The aircraft relies on jet propulsion to reach high speeds.
Engineers are testing a new propulsion system for the rocket.

definition: the activity of searching an area for gold, oil, or other minerals

collocations.example: Thousands of people went prospecting for gold in the mountains.
They developed a new prospecting method to locate oil deposits.

definition: a printed document that describes a company, school, or plan to attract people

collocations.example: Investors studied the company prospectus before buying any shares.
She requested the college prospectus to learn about available courses.

definition: the place that something originally came from; its origin or history

collocations.example: The painting was of unknown provenance and hard to value.
Experts questioned the provenance of the ancient gold coins.

definition: a condition that must be accepted as part of an agreement

collocations.example: She agreed to the visit, with the proviso that it stay short.
The bank attached a proviso to the loan agreement.

definition: a serious mental illness in which a person loses touch with reality

collocations.example: After the trauma, he began to suffer from psychosis.
Doctors treated her for a severe form of psychosis.

definition: relating to both the mind and a person's social relationships

collocations.example: Doctors considered the psychosocial factors behind the patient's stress.
The hospital offers psychosocial support to families of patients.

definition: the stage when a child's body develops into an adult's and becomes able to reproduce

collocations.example: Children usually reach puberty between the ages of ten and fourteen.
The onset of puberty often brings many emotional changes.

definition: a small, very dense star that sends out regular pulses of radio waves

collocations.example: Astronomers discovered a millisecond pulsar spinning hundreds of times a second.
The radio telescope was able to detect a distant pulsar.

definition: to move or beat with a strong, regular rhythm

collocations.example: The whole city seemed to pulsate with energy at night.
The warning light continued to pulsate steadily in the dark.

definition: in American football, a player whose job is to kick the ball to the other team

collocations.example: The team's punter kicked the ball sixty yards downfield.
A good punter kicks the ball high to give teammates time.

definition: a small bag used to carry money and personal items

collocations.example: She bought a small leather purse for the trip.
She kept her keys and phone in her purse.

definition: in accordance with a law, rule, or agreement

collocations.example: The company must report its earnings pursuant to the law.
Payment will be made pursuant to the agreement signed last month.

definition: to provide or sell food, goods, or services

collocations.example: The market stalls purvey goods from farms across the region.
The website purveys information about local events and festivals.

definition: generally believed or supposed to be something

collocations.example: A DNA test confirmed that he was the putative father.
Researchers identified a putative cause of the rare disease.

definition: a person who dishonestly pretends to have medical knowledge or skill

collocations.example: A quack doctor sold the villagers a useless, overpriced medicine.
Other scientists dismissed him as a quack after the experiment failed.

definition: an open square area with buildings around it, especially at a school or college

collocations.example: Students gathered in the college quad between their morning classes.
She hurried across the quad to reach the library before noon.

definition: a feeling of doubt or worry about whether something is right

collocations.example: She had no qualms about telling him the honest truth.
He spent the entire budget without a single qualm.

definition: a period of time when a person or animal is kept apart to stop disease from spreading

collocations.example: The sick passengers were put in quarantine for two weeks.
Imported animals must complete a strict quarantine period before entering.

definition: a hard mineral used in making glass, watches, and electronics

collocations.example: The watch keeps accurate time using a tiny quartz crystal.
He bought a reliable quartz watch for everyday use.

definition: to put an end to something, such as rumors, doubts, or opposition

collocations.example: The company issued a statement to quash rumors of layoffs.
The government sent troops to quash the growing rebellion.

definition: a solid platform beside water where boats are loaded and unloaded

collocations.example: A large crowd was waiting on the quay for the ferry.
Several fishing boats were moored to the quay overnight.

definition: being the most perfect or typical example of something

collocations.example: This dish is the quintessential example of traditional Italian cooking.
With his fast talk and energy, he was the quintessential New Yorker.

definition: a way of raising money by selling numbered tickets, with prizes for the winners

collocations.example: She bought a raffle ticket hoping to win the new car.
The school will hold a raffle to raise money for books.

definition: a period of wild, violent, and destructive behavior

collocations.example: Angry crowds went on a rampage through the city center.
Police arrested the man after his violent rampage downtown.

definition: a feeling of extreme joy and delight

collocations.example: The children listened with rapture as she told the story.
Critics went into raptures over the young singer's performance.

definition: loud, rough, and often disorderly

collocations.example: Raucous laughter came from the table in the corner.
A raucous crowd cheered loudly as the home team scored.

definition: a deep, narrow valley with steep sides

collocations.example: The car skidded off the road and plunged into a ravine.
A narrow bridge crossed the deep ravine below the village.

definition: an unkind or sharp refusal of a friendly offer or request

collocations.example: Her offer of help was met with a sharp rebuff.
His request for more time met with a firm rebuff.

definition: to prove that a statement or accusation is false

collocations.example: She prepared evidence to rebut her opponent's main argument.
The company quickly moved to rebut the serious allegation.

definition: to do or give something in return for something you have received

collocations.example: He loved her deeply, but she did not reciprocate his feelings.
They sent us a gift, so we reciprocated the kind gesture.

definition: the practice of exchanging things with others for mutual benefit

collocations.example: Good friendships are built on a spirit of reciprocity.
The trade deal is based on reciprocity between the two nations.

definition: a person who lives alone and avoids other people

collocations.example: After his wife died, he became a complete recluse.
The famous author lived as a virtual recluse for decades.

definition: to get back money that you have spent or lost

collocations.example: The investors hoped to recoup their losses within a year.
It took five years to recoup the initial investment fully.

definition: relating to the rectum, the lower end of the bowel

collocations.example: The doctor recommended a rectal examination to check for problems.
Early screening can help detect rectal cancer before it spreads.

definition: to get better after an illness or a period of tiredness

collocations.example: She took two weeks off to recuperate from the illness.
He went to the countryside to rest and recuperate.

definition: to have a strong, unpleasant smell

collocations.example: His clothes reeked of smoke after the long bonfire.
The locker room reeked of sweat after the match.

definition: a surface or object that reflects light, heat, or radio waves

collocations.example: A red reflector on the bike made it visible at night.
The satellite dish uses a parabolic reflector to focus signals.

definition: a condition in which acid from the stomach flows back up into the throat

collocations.example: Spicy food often gives him painful acid reflux at night.
Many patients suffer from reflux after eating large meals.

definition: to fill a vehicle or aircraft with fuel again

collocations.example: The plane had to stop to refuel in Hawaii.
Ground crews worked quickly to refuel the aircraft before takeoff.

definition: a type of popular music from Jamaica with a strong, regular beat

collocations.example: He grew up listening to reggae music from Jamaica.
A local reggae band played at the beach festival.

definition: a type of deer with large antlers that lives in cold northern regions

collocations.example: A herd of reindeer crossed the frozen northern plain.
In the story, the sleigh is pulled by eight reindeer.

definition: to publish or make something available again

collocations.example: The band decided to reissue their first album on vinyl.

definition: to make someone or something feel or look young, fresh, or lively again

collocations.example: The cream claims to rejuvenate tired, aging skin overnight.
The city spent millions to rejuvenate the old industrial neighborhood.

definition: to send someone accused of a crime back into custody or release them on bail until trial

collocations.example: The judge decided to remand the suspect in custody.
She was remanded on bail until her trial next month.

definition: to pay someone for work they have done or services they have provided

collocations.example: The firm agreed to remunerate the consultants for their work.
Senior engineers at the company are very well remunerated.

definition: a performance or version of a song, play, or piece of music

collocations.example: The band played a lively rendition of an old folk song.
She gave a stirring rendition of the national anthem.
